note: This workflow's own gate stack. Run `gates` from this directory: it verifies the vendored tooling, not a project.

gates.name: vendored
gates.why: the vendored tools are the version recorded in tools/vendored.sha256, and no older than the kit's — a copy that drifts silently is the failure the manifest exists to catch (tools/VENDORED.md)

gates.name: syntax
gates.run: python3 -m py_compile tools/crap tools/depth tools/gates tools/mutate-changed checks/test_crap.py checks/test_depth.py checks/test_gates.py checks/test_mutate_changed.py && bash -n install.sh && bash -n setup.sh && bash -n tools/sync-from-kit.sh
gates.why: the tools and the scripts parse

gates.name: crap
gates.why: the CRAP metric matches its hand-computed values

gates.name: mutate-changed
gates.why: the scoped mutation run decides what to mutate and which tests to run before Stryker starts, and each of those decisions is pinned to the failure it prevents: the config's own exclusions (a scoped run that ignores them reports survivors nobody can kill), a cache key per scope (a shared one reuses a scoped run's survivors as truth), and a tree left instrumented by an aborted run (the next run's dry run then fails, which reads as a broken suite)

gates.name: depth
gates.why: the nine decidable red flags match the book they came from: 12 findings on its flawed examples, 6 in Python, 0 on its corrected ones, plus the five cross-module flags and the six readings, each with its negative beside it
